original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Construct a globally executable 32-chain per-target-order schedule attaining Ali Romman's PR1125 lower bound for the exact 104-port, eight-centre fixture in PR1071/biframe-decoder-ladder. Certify all chronological frame moves and the complete supplied-copy tail invoice; do not claim the existing 32 lower bound as new.
scope_change_reason: The emitted card asks for a new block decoder and a complete supplier gain. The source-pinned P104 decoder already saves eight copy ranks but its delivery is unresolved. The investigation changes PR1071's global-order restriction. Final merged/local overlap revealed PR1125 already proves the stronger asynchronous 32-path obstruction, while explicitly excluding schedule attainment; the new contribution is the attaining witness and tail invoice only. No complete supplier or five-percent acceptance claim is made.
bottleneck_link: The P104 decoder has copy rank 56 instead of 64, but incompatible survivor frames require additional delivery arrays. Reducing the exact chain count and pricing its monotone paths addresses this concrete barrier rather than repacking the selected word.
stop_rule: Analyze the one pinned P104 fixture only; use bounded combinatorial synthesis with exact independently checked certificates. Stop with an exact geometric construction or obstruction, not an unpriced physical supplier.
evidence: SCHEDULE.json gives 116 exact prefix edges and 32 chains. RESULT.json binds all 10816 decoder entries, 14400 binary pairings, eight rank-seven drops, 416 chronological reads, the 32-element rank-four antichain, complete supplied-boundary tail profiles, interval prices and eight controls. The supplied-copy dirty-state limitation is tested on every chain.

optimistic_budget: Inherited COPY56 remains. At the explicit boundary of 32 exact copies already at singleton survivor frames, delivery tails cost {1:85,2:17,3:19,4:20} (mass256), target tails {1:416,2:12,3:24,4:32,5:24,6:12} (mass832), and 416 scalar reads remain. Formation of 24 extra exact copies, gather, restoration, side corrections, hosting and precision are explicit unknown nonzero obligations. The selected-word ceiling is not applied to this incomplete interface.
success_falsification: Success: an exact executable 32-chain schedule attaining the credited PR1125 lower bound, with all chronological and frame constraints. Falsification: an omitted/duplicated read, nonnested chain, cyclic dependency, failed decoder identity or hidden uncharged physical operation.
